title.narrative: 2022 - 2025 Project on Tax Administration, STA - GDT
2022 - 2025 Samarbetsprojekt om skatteförvaltning mellan STA och GDT

description.narrative:
The main Objective of the Project is to support the General Directorate of Tax in Albania in achieving the development and progress needed based on the Medium Term Revenue Strategy 2022-2026. To support this desired change, there will be three Project Objectives:
1. Improve Good Governance: - The GDT has improved its capacity to promote good governance by e.g. improve efficiency and accountability in business and prevent corruption. - The GDT has started to analyse and tackle, wherever possible, the gender issues identified within the taxpayers community and also the tax administrations employees.
2. Strengthen Voluntary Compliance: - The GDT has strengthened its capacity to plan, prioritize and organize work processes based on Voluntary Compliance.
3. Strengthen Business Development & Capacity Development: - The GDT has strengthened its business development processes and its capacity development
Att stödja den albanska skattemyndigheten i att uppnå utvecklingsframsteg för att stärka god förvaltning, frivillig efterlevnad och affärsutveckling.

To support Albanian Tax Authority in achieving development progress on strengthening good governance, voluntary compliance and business development. The appraisal is about the starting of the longer cooperaiton between the General Directorate of Taxation in Albania (GDT) and the Swedish Tax Agency (STA) with the aim to strengthen the domestic revenue mobilization for 2022 - 2025. The three-year cooperation will be financed by the Sweden International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida). The GDT and STA has gone through a fact finding and inception phase for almost two years. The preparation phase of the cooperation was important for the parties to get to know better each other, assess needs and gaps, identify the areas of support, establish a project managment structure. In addition, during this period some acitivities had started in the prioritized areas. The main Objective of the Project is to support the GDT in achieving the development and progress needed based on the Albanian Medium Term Strategy (MTRS) 2022-2026. The Project will support these advances by focusing on strengthening good governance, voluntary compliance, and business development within the GDT. This Project will indirectly contribute to the European Union (EU) integration process of Albania and will lay foundations for addressing the European Commission´s recommendation under Chapter 16 (Taxation) related to readiness to apply the EU Information Technology (IT) systems such as Value Added Tax Information Exchange System (VIES). The Project consists of five components: i) To build a strong Integrity Culture; ii) To improve Compliance Risk Management; iii) To improve Taxpayer Service; iv) To strengthen the Tax Audit function; and v) To improve and develop business processes. STA is a Swedish agency, committed partner to Swedish Development and Sida but also to the Albanian Government and GDPT. STA has cooperated with GDT for 2004 - 2012 through EU funding. The GDT has shown full commitment to this cooperation allocating also the necessary resources to the project.

description.narrative:
During the third project year (November 2024 October 2025), the cooperation between the General Directorate of Taxation (GDT) and the Swedish Tax Agency (STA) continued to build on piloting and method development, while gradually strengthening consolidation and application of established approaches.
- Within Integrity Culture, the trainthetrainer model matured into a scalable and contextsensitive approach for promoting ethical awareness and dialogue across the Tax Administration. Internal Audit activities resumed and generated shared understanding of the audit functions role in anticorruption, aligned with international standards.
- The Compliance Risk Management (CRM) component advanced from operational pilots to more strategic application. Monthly Risk Committee meetings with senior management participation improved coordination and holistic risk governance. The development of General Risk Overview (GRO) concepts and continued work on a pilot targeting newly registered businesses strengthened GDTs capacity to identify, assess and evaluate compliance risks.
- In Taxpayer Service, progress was achieved on both strategic and operational levels. A draft Service Strategy was developed as a longterm framework for citizen centred service delivery. Operationally, requirements for a modernised call centre were specified, providing the basis for a forthcoming technical upgrade. A second nationwide taxpayer survey reinforced the importance of systematic user feedback, while plain language initiatives continued to improve clarity and accessibility in communication. Together, these efforts strengthened GDTs orientation towards taxpayer needs and voluntary compliance.
- The Tax Audit component focused on building sustainable training capacity, particularly within the tourism sector. Through a structured train the trainer approach, GDT audit staff strengthened both pedagogical and technical skills, including active learning methods and clearer training design. Work on platform economy audits and regional knowledge sharing further enhanced audit capability. By the end of the period, GDT teams demonstrated strong ownership of training frameworks, indicating reduced reliance on external expertise.
- Within Business Processes, including AEOI/CRS, the focus shifted towards quality, compliance and readiness. In the AEOI/CRS subcomponent, emphasis was placed on improving outgoing data quality and strengthening engagement with financial institutions. Risk based approaches and cross departmental collaboration increased GDTs confidence and preparedness for future use of exchanged data and EU related requirements.
- The Business Development subcomponent delivered a visible result through the launch of the web based Tax Test, developed using service design principles. The service contributed to higher than expected income tax return filings and demonstrated the effectiveness of rapid, usercentric and low cost development methods.
